sections.overview: Apistogramma regani is a small freshwater cichlid described by Sven Kullander in 1980 and named for British ichthyologist Charles Tate Regan.
sections.identification: FishBase lists 4.9 cm standard length for male or unsexed fish and 5.0 cm for females, without specifying the female convention; it also gives a maximum published mass of 2.29 g. No reliable body width or height measurement was found. The fish has clear abdominal stripes and a striped caudal fin.
sections.habitat: The documented range is in the lower Rio Negro basin, within the Amazon drainage. FishBase describes a freshwater, bottom-associated tropical fish and reports water temperatures around 23–30 °C in the available account.
sections.diet: No species-specific diet study was found. Like related dwarf cichlids, it is expected to pick small invertebrates from the bottom, but this remains a genus-level inference rather than a measured menu.
sections.behavior: Cichlid Room Companion describes the species as polygynous and a harem-brooder. This is an aquarium reference, not a detailed study of wild group structure.
sections.reproduction: The female tends eggs attached to a cave ceiling and cares for the larvae. FishBase provides no clutch-size range for this species.
sections.ecology: Apistogramma regani belongs to the informal regani group. Compared with the related A. resticulosa, it has distinct abdominal stripes rather than short dark dashes; both species have a striped caudal fin, so that mark alone is not enough.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern, assessed on 29 October 2020. The cited field guide gives the same status and assessment date.
